subject: Trial governance & infra handshake — GreenEdge pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@greenedge.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial governance & infra handshake — GreenEdge pilot

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier. Thanks for the deep product walkthrough. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned for the pilot: 

Summary of success criteria (what GreenEdge will consider the trial successful):
- Baseline throughput: sustain 200 inference requests/minute with p95 latency < 350ms for 1k token responses.
- Quality: average prompt-to-expected similarity score > 0.82 on the provided eval set (see tab "Gold Prompts").
- Integration: embeddings + reranking pipeline integrated into staging app and validated end-to-end.
- Security/compliance: access logs and KMS key usage available to your SOC team for review.

Proposed ownership (high-level):
- GreenEdge infra (VPC peering, firewall rules, network prep): GreenEdge infra team / procurement to approve.
- App integration (SDK + request shaping): Alicia & app engineering.
- Security & audit evidence: Neha (Redwood) to coordinate evidence package; GreenEdge SOC to request docs.
- Sales & escalation: me (Jonas) — point for scheduling and contract items.

Immediate next steps:
1) Alicia to share names/emails for infra and procurement leads and confirm availability for a short infra handshake call this week.
2) Neha will send the POC success criteria workbook and a proposed 3-week evaluation timeline.
3) I’ll open a HubSpot record and attach the plan, then add procurement thread with the finance contact if needed.

Attachments: GreenEdge_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (initial draft), network_requirements.pdf (network checklist).

If that all looks right I’ll loop everyone and schedule the 30-minute infra handshake.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192

From: Alicia Torres <alicia@greenedge.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, procurement@greenedge.io
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial governance & infra handshake — GreenEdge pilot

Thanks Jonas — that summary is helpful. A few tidbits from our side: 
- Confirmed success criteria look good; we'll validate against our bench test harness.
- Procurement: please include procurement@greenedge.io on any contract/commitment communications. They will own the SLAs and PO.
- Infra contact: putting our infra lead in copy on the next note (cc'd above). They will need network requirements and an expected maintenance window.

Question: for the pilot does Redwood need VPC peering or would an egress-restricted NAT approach work? We prefer to avoid full peering if possible. Also, can you confirm if logging can be routed to our Splunk token over HTTPS?

I can be available for a 30-min call Thursday morning PT. If that works for Neha and your team, let's lock it.

Best,
Alicia Torres
Head of Product, GreenEdge
alicia@greenedge.io

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@greenedge.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, procurement@greenedge.io
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial governance & infra handshake — GreenEdge pilot

Hi Alicia / team — looping in some specifics so the infra handshake call is productive. Attached is a draft POC workbook (GreenEdge_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx) with the evaluation plan and a simple RACI grid. Key points below and proposed 3-week schedule.

Inline RACI (summary):
- Owner (GreenEdge): app integration for embeddings & reranker, acceptance of quality.
- Responsible (Redwood): runtime provisioning, model variant configuration, observability/tracing hooks for token-level costing.
- Consulted (GreenEdge SOC / Redwood security): evidence exchange (SOC2 report excerpts, audit logs), KMS integration plan.
- Informed: procurement, platform ops.

Security & network notes: 
- Preferred: egress-restricted NAT + TLS to Redwood endpoints is sufficient for the pilot — avoids VPC peering. We can support IP allowlisting for your NAT gateway.
- Splunk: we can push request/response metadata and audit logs to your HTTPS endpoint via a secure ingestion token. We do not log raw PII by default; audit logs contain request IDs and metadata required for traceability.

Proposed 3-week timeline: 
Week 0 (Prep, 3–5 business days): network checklist, add IPs to allowlist, procurement paperwork (if needed).
Week 1 (Integration, 5 business days): SDK integration, test harness run, baseline metrics captured.
Week 2 (Load & quality, 5 business days): scaled traffic window, quality regression checks on shared prompts.
Week 3 (Wrap & handoff, 3 business days): final report, handoff doc, contract/next steps.

Deliverables we will provide: POC workbook (attached), a lightweight runbook for troubleshooting, and a Redwood support contact for on-call during the scaled window.

Can we confirm:
1) GreenEdge will own adding our IPs to their allowlist and providing a Splunk ingestion token by Thursday EOD.
2) Procurement to confirm the PO timeline or whether a mutual NDA/short MSA is required before we begin.

I attached the workbook and network checklist: GreenEdge_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx; network_requirements.pdf

Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@greenedge.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial governance & infra handshake — GreenEdge pilot

Alicia — quick follow up after reviewing the workbook. Two clarifications before the infra call: 
1) IP ranges: Neha, can you confirm the list of egress IP ranges we need to add? Having them in CIDR form helps our infra team schedule the change.
2) Firewall/NAT behaviors: if GreenEdge will use egress NAT, we need a stable public IP or small CIDR block so we can map rate-limiting and the token-based audit logs reliably. Without that, we're forced to fallback to per-request signing which adds integration complexity.

On the Splunk ingestion: we support HTTPS ingestion with a short-lived token; GreenEdge ops will need to provide a URL and token during Week 0.

If Thursday morning PT is good I’ll join the call and run through the network checklist live — should take 25–30 minutes.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
